newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba, Ruhrgas plan telecoms link-up - paper.
newsitem.headline: Veba, Ruhrgas plan telecoms link-up - paper.

text.p: Diversified German utility VEBA AG plans a telecommunications link-up with Ruhrgas, the country's largest gas company, Germany's Handelsblatt newspaper said on Monday, citing unnamed sources.
The newspaper said VEBA wanted to use Ruhrgas's broad cable network for its own telecommunications purposes and was close to signing a contract on the deal.
However the newspaper noted that Vebacom, VEBA's telecoms unit, had described the report as speculative.
Veba was not immediately available for comment.
Ruhrgas has 10,000 km of cable which is currently only used internally. It has already said it is in talks with several potential partners in telecommunications, including Vebacom.
Handelsblatt also said VEBA's contract would entail use of the east German gas firm Verbundnetz Gas AG's network. Ruhrgas owns 35 percent of the Verbundnetz.

The newspaper said VEBA was forced to take action to access a network after rival telecoms provider Mannesmann AG agreed in July to take a major stake in DBKom GmbH, the communications subsidiary of the German railway.
